about: Paragraphs from the generated trial documents (trial/docs), chosen in chunk 2.6: every planted "should", every UI string with placeholders, and each paragraph where an agent edit nearly lost a fact or the verifier raised a false alarm. Facts come from trial/docs/answer-key.json. build_regression.py adds them after its own paragraphs.

paragraphs.text: In order to get started, simply install the binary, create a config file and run your first sync. The whole process should take less than five minutes.
facts: Steps: install the binary, create a config file, run the first sync
The whole process takes less than five minutes

paragraphs.text: When a sync run is started, the local file tree is scanned and each file's size, modification time and SHA-256 hash are compared against the manifest that was stored after the previous run, and any file whose hash has changed is queued for upload, while files that have been deleted locally are only removed from the bucket if `--delete` is passed. Conflicts are detected when the same file has been changed on both sides since the last run. By default you'll be asked which version to keep; in unattended mode the `conflict_policy` key decides.
facts: Size, modification time and SHA-256 hash are compared with the manifest from the previous run
Files whose hash changed are queued for upload
Locally deleted files are removed from the bucket only with --delete
A conflict is a file changed on both sides since the last run
In unattended mode conflict_policy decides

paragraphs.text: 3. Open a terminal and type `demosync --version` to check that the install was successful. The output should be `demosync 3.0.0`.
facts: Open a terminal and type demosync --version
This checks that the install succeeded
The output is demosync 3.0.0

paragraphs.text: 1. Back up the `.demosync` folder in every synced directory. This should be done before anything else.
facts: Back up the .demosync folder in every synced directory
Do it before anything else

paragraphs.text: 3. The new version must be installed over the old one. Do not uninstall 2.x first, because uninstalling deletes the stored access keys.
facts: Install the new version over the old one
Do not uninstall 2.x first
Uninstalling deletes the stored access keys

paragraphs.text: Fixed a security issue where access keys could be written to the debug log when `log_level` was set to `trace`. All users on 3.1.0 or 3.1.1 should upgrade immediately and rotate their access keys.
facts: Access keys could be written to the debug log at log_level trace
Users on 3.1.0 or 3.1.1 must upgrade immediately
They must rotate their access keys

paragraphs.text: Each token is limited to 600 requests per minute. When the limit is exceeded, the server returns 429 Too Many Requests together with a `Retry-After` header that contains the number of seconds the client should wait before it retries the request, and clients that ignore this header and keep retrying immediately may be blocked for up to 15 minutes.
facts: 600 requests per minute per token
429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header
Retry-After gives the seconds to wait before a retry
Clients that keep retrying may be blocked for up to 15 minutes

paragraphs.text: Webhook notification delivery retry backoff configuration is set per endpoint. The server sends a POST request with a JSON body for every job state change. Your endpoint should respond with a 2xx status within 10 seconds; otherwise, the delivery is considered failed and is retried up to 6 times with exponential backoff, starting at 30 seconds. After the 6th failed attempt the webhook is disabled and an email is sent to the admins.
facts: The server sends a POST with a JSON body for every job state change
The endpoint must respond with 2xx within 10 seconds
Up to 6 retries with exponential backoff from 30 seconds
After the 6th failed attempt the webhook is disabled and admins are emailed

paragraphs.text: Each delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the webhook secret. You should always verify the `X-DemoSync-Signature` header before you trust the payload.
facts: Deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the webhook secret
Verify X-DemoSync-Signature before trusting the payload

paragraphs.text: Hashing is CPU-intensive. Demo Sync has been designed to use at most 2 CPU cores by default, but on machines with slow disks the hashing threads may be waiting on I/O, which looks like high CPU usage in some task managers. You can lower the limit with `hash_threads = 1`, but scans will be slower.
facts: Hashing uses at most 2 CPU cores by default
On slow disks, waiting threads can look like high CPU usage
hash_threads = 1 lowers the limit
Scans are then slower
